facts.statement: Fossils of Gorgonichthys were found in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shales of Ohio.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shales of Late Devonian in Ohio.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shales of Ohio, United States.
facts.quote: Los fósiles se encontraron en las lutitas de Cleveland del periodo Famenniano superior del Devónico tardío en Ohio, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: With a headshield length of up to 70 centimeters, Gorgonichthys is estimated to have been comparable in total size to Dunkleosteus.
facts.quote: Con una longitud del escudo craneal de hasta 70 centímetros (28 pulgadas), se estima que en vida su longitud total era comparable al tamaño de Dunkleosteus.

facts.statement: Gorgonichthys is an extinct, monospecific genus of large arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Gorgonichthys is extinct monospecific genus of large arthrodire placoderm.

facts.statement: Gorgonichthys belongs to the order Arthrodira.
Gorgonichthys is classified within the unranked family Aspinothoracidi.
A 2022 study by Jobbins et al. suggests Gorgonichthys is more closely related to Heintzichthys than Gymnotrachelus, potentially making it a member of the family Selenosteidae.
facts.quote: According to a 2022 Jobbins et al. study, Gorgonichthys was found to be more related to Heintzichthys than Gymnotrachelus, potentially making Gorgonichthys a member of Selenosteidae.

facts.statement: Un estudio de 2022 de Jobbins et al. descubrió que Gorgonichthys estaba más relacionado con Heintzichthys que con Gymnotrachelus, lo que potencialmente lo convertiría en un miembro de Selenosteidae.

facts.statement: Gorgonichthys lived during the Late Devonian period, specifically the Upper Famennian.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Upper Famennian Cleveland Shales of Late Devonian in Ohio.

facts.statement: Gorgonichthys lived between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (372.15 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gorgonichthys is Gorgonichthys clarki.
facts.quote: The type species is Gorgonichthys clarki.

facts.statement: The type species is Gorgonichthys clarki, described by Claypole in 1892.
Fossil specimens of Gorgonichthys include infragnatal plates (lower jaws) that are scaled against a 1-liter water bottle measuring approximately 23 cm in height.
